features.heading: Engineered for Performance
features.subtitle: The feature set you need to analyze data without the bloat.

groupBy.title: Group-by Summary
groupBy.description: Summarize data by any column in seconds. Select a range, choose your category and value columns, and get instant roll-ups with SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, and COUNT — no pivot-table setup.
groupBy.bullet1: Multi-level grouping across up to 6 columns
groupBy.bullet2: Instant SUM / AVG / MIN / MAX / COUNT on any range selection

formats.title: Wide Format Support
formats.description: Open your spreadsheets directly — no conversion, no setup.

multiSheet.title: Multi-sheet Navigation
multiSheet.description: Switch between worksheet tabs in any workbook from the bottom tab bar.

command.title: Command Palette
command.description: Cmd+K to jump to any cell reference or run an action — keyboard-first navigation.

virtualized.title: Virtualized Rendering
virtualized.description: LazySheet only renders the rows you can see. Scroll through massive sheets with smooth, lag-free movement regardless of hardware.

filters.title: Column Filters
filters.description: Click the funnel on any header. 14 filter types plus an Excel-style value checklist.

sticky.title: Sticky Header Row
sticky.description: Mark any row as the header — it stays pinned while you scroll through the data.

resize.title: Resizable Columns & Rows
resize.description: Drag to resize, double-click to autofit. Sizes are remembered per file.

format.title: Rich Cell Formatting
format.description: Fonts, colors, alignment, merged cells, and clickable hyperlinks preserved from .xlsx files.

copy.title: Copy as Image
copy.description: Capture a group-by summary report as a PNG straight to your clipboard.

find.title: Find in Sheet
find.description: Full-text search with Cmd+F. Jump between matches highlighted across the sheet.

native.title: Native macOS Integration
native.description: Drag & drop, 'Open With', and Recent Files support built in.

faq.heading: Having trouble opening the app?
faq.subtitle: Common questions about installing LazySheet.
faq.unsignedQuestion: macOS says LazySheet is "damaged" or from an "unidentified developer"
faq.unsignedAnswerPre: LazySheet isn't code-signed with an Apple Developer certificate yet, so macOS Gatekeeper quarantines it and blocks it from opening. The app is safe — you just need to remove the quarantine flag. Open the
faq.unsignedAnswerPost: After it finishes, open LazySheet normally from Applications. If you installed it elsewhere, change the path to match its location.

guide.pageDescription: Learn how to open, browse, filter, and analyze spreadsheets with LazySheet in nine quick steps.
guide.heading: How to use LazySheet
guide.subtitle: Open a file and start analyzing in seconds — no setup, no formulas required.

open.title: Open any file
open.body: Press ⌘O to open the file picker, or simply drag and drop a file onto the window. LazySheet supports xlsx, xls, csv, and tsv — no conversion needed.
open.alt: Native file picker showing CSV files in Downloads folder

browse.title: Browse instantly
browse.body: Your data loads in milliseconds. Scroll through hundreds of thousands of rows with zero lag — every column visible at a glance, exactly as it appears in the source file.
browse.alt: Full data grid displaying all columns of a large CSV file

setheader.title: Set the header row
setheader.body: Right-click any row and choose "Mark as header" to promote it to your column headers — perfect for exports where the real header sits a few rows down. The grid relabels instantly.
setheader.alt: Row context menu with the "Mark as header" option open over the data grid

filter.title: Filter columns
filter.body: Click any column header's filter icon to open the filter popover. Pick specific values from a searchable list, or set a condition like "greater than" or "contains" to narrow down your data instantly.
filter.alt: Column filter popover with searchable value checkboxes and condition options

stats.title: Instant stats
stats.body: Select any range of cells and the status bar at the bottom shows live aggregate stats — SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, and COUNT — without writing a single formula.
stats.alt: Selection stats bar showing SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, and COUNT for selected cells

groupby.title: Group-by & aggregate
groupby.body: Open "Summarize selection" to aggregate one column grouped by another — choose SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, or COUNT. Then copy the result as Markdown or TSV to paste straight into your notes, docs, or a message.
groupby.alt: Group-by summary panel with aggregate options and Copy Markdown / Copy TSV buttons

copyformats.title: Copy in any format
copyformats.body: Select a range or a summary and copy it as Markdown, TSV, or even an Image. Paste straight into your docs, a chat message, or a web form — no reformatting, no export dialog.
copyformats.alt: Copy menu open showing Markdown, TSV, and Image format options

dragout.title: Drag out to any app
dragout.body: Drag the open file straight from LazySheet into a browser upload zone, a chat window, or any app that accepts file drops. No "Save As", no temp files — just grab and drop.
dragout.alt: Dragging the spreadsheet file from LazySheet into a CloudConvert drop zone in the browser

command.title: Command palette
command.body: Press ⌘P (or click the search bar) to open the command palette. Quickly jump to a cell with Goto, run Summarize selection (⌘⇧Y), Copy file, Copy file path, or Open a new file — all from the keyboard.
command.alt: Command palette showing Goto, Summarize selection, Copy file, Copy file path, and Open file commands
